physics_detail: Nuclear binding energy: energy required to completely separate nucleus into free protons and neutrons; semi-empirical mass formula (Bethe-Weizsäcker): BE = a_V×A - a_S×A^(2/3) - a_C×Z(Z-1)/A^(1/3) - a_A×(N-Z)²/A + δ_pairing; peak: Fe-56 at 8.79 MeV/nucleon; fission (U-235 → Sr-90 + Xe-143): products more tightly bound; energy released = difference in binding energy ≈ 200 MeV per fission; fusion (H→He): lighter nuclei also less tightly bound → energy released
chernobyl_quantum_relevance: 200 MeV per U-235 fission: 3200 MWth RBMK reactor → 1.0×10²⁰ fissions per second; each fission releases 200 MeV = 3.2×10⁻¹¹ J; U-235 specific fission rate at 3200 MWth = 3.2×10¹⁰/3.2×10⁻¹¹ = 10^21 fissions/second; in 10 years RBMK operation = 10^29 fissions total; binding energy curve explains why fission products (near N=50, N=82 shell closures) are most abundant
source: Bethe Weizsäcker 1935; Blatt Weisskopf 1952; INSAG-7 Appendix; fission_product_yields_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Nuclear shell model (Mayer Jensen 1949): nucleons fill discrete energy levels analogous to electron shells; magic proton/neutron numbers: 2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126; nuclei with magic N or Z have extra stability; spin-orbit coupling lifts degeneracy; magic numbers explain bimodal fission yield distribution: light peak (N=50, Z≈38=Sr) and heavy peak (N=82, Z≈55=Cs) have enhanced stability as fission fragments; valley between peaks corresponds to symmetric fission (symmetric unstable because neither fragment has magic numbers)
chernobyl_quantum_relevance: N=50 shell closure: determines why A≈90-95 mass region (including Sr-90, Zr-95) dominates light fission product peak; N=82 shell closure: determines why A≈133-140 mass region (including Cs-137, Ba-140, I-131, Xe-133) dominates heavy peak; magic number stability = fundamental quantum explanation for WHY Cs-137 and Sr-90 are the dominant long-lived radiological hazards from Chernobyl
source: Mayer 1949 Phys Rev; Jensen 1949; Strutinsky 1967 Nucl Phys A 95:420; fission_product_yields_REAL.csv; radioactive_decay_chains_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Breit-Wigner single-level formula: σ(E) = π×ƛ² × g × (Γ_n×Γ)/(E-E_r)²+(Γ/2)²; where E_r = resonance energy; Γ = total width; Γ_n = neutron width; g = statistical spin factor; ƛ = reduced de Broglie wavelength; resonance cross sections can reach 10³-10⁶ barns; Xe-135 giant resonance at E~0.084 eV (near thermal energy): σ_max ≈ 4×10⁶ barns
chernobyl_quantum_relevance: Xe-135 cross section 2.65×10⁶ barns at thermal energy = sum of multiple resonance contributions (but dominated by single strong resonance at 0.084 eV = thermal energy); this is physically why Xe-135 is the most powerful reactor poison: its quantum mechanical resonance energy exactly coincides with the thermal neutron spectrum; accidental quantum alignment; no other nucleus has such a large cross section at thermal energy
source: Breit Wigner 1936 Phys Rev 49:519; Mughabghab 1984 Neutron Cross Sections; xenon_135_poisoning_REAL.csv; rbmk_core_neutron_physics_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Doppler broadening mechanism (quantum explanation): U-238 resonance absorption at ~6.67 eV; stationary nucleus: sharp resonance (Breit-Wigner); thermal motion of U-238 atoms at temperature T (Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution): each atom has different kinetic energy → in COM frame, neutron energy shifted; nuclear reaction cross section must be folded with velocity distribution; result: resonance appears broadened to observer; width increases as √T; area conserved (same total absorption probability); higher T → broader resonance → more absorption
chernobyl_quantum_relevance: Doppler broadening: as fuel temperature increases: more U-238 atoms in tail of velocity distribution; more overlap between neutron thermal spectrum and broadened U-238 resonance; more U-238 absorptions (n,γ → U-239 → Pu-239; not fission); fewer neutrons available; negative reactivity feedback INSTANTANEOUS (responds at speed of heat transfer ~microseconds, not seconds); this is why reactors are FUNDAMENTALLY self-limiting against transients that cause fuel heating
source: Glasstone Sesonske; Wigner ORNL 1946; Blatt Weisskopf 1952; rbmk_void_coefficient_physics_REAL.csv; rbmk_core_neutron_physics_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Radioactive decay law: N(t) = N₀ × exp(-λt); activity A = λN = A₀ × exp(-λt); decay constant λ = ln2/t½; quantum mechanical basis: decay is tunneling of alpha particle (or weak force beta decay) through Coulomb barrier; probability per unit time (λ) = constant because: quantum tunneling probability depends only on barrier width/height (fixed by nuclear structure); each nucleus decays independently; no memory of past; decay law is EXACT quantum prediction

physics_detail: Pair production: photon → e⁻ + e⁺; requires E_γ ≥ 2m_e c² = 2 × 0.511 MeV = 1.022 MeV; QED (quantum electrodynamics) process; occurs in Coulomb field of nucleus; cross section increases with E_γ above threshold; σ_pp ∝ Z² × ln(E_γ/m_e c²) at high energy; positron rapidly annihilates with electron → two 511 keV annihilation photons (back-to-back; momentum conservation); signature: 511 keV peak in gamma spectrum
